articles.title_orig: Written in bone: China bets on ancient scripts for modern soft power
articles.title_zh: Written in bone: China bets on ancient scripts for modern soft power
articles.content_orig:
New institute dedicated to preserving rare and endangered historical disciplines advances Beijing’s push to elevate traditional culture
The institute was inaugurated at the University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (UCASS) in Beijing on Friday, alongside the launch of an association to consolidate nationwide resources involving the studies.
The institute includes a dozen ancient ethnic minority scripts such as Tangut and Old Tibetan, whose surviving texts provide insights into the histories of northwestern China border regions, as well as oracle bone inscriptions dating back more than 3,000 years and representing the country’s earliest known fully developed writing system.

articles.title_orig: Israel’s newly elected parliament is already moving against Netanyahu
articles.title_zh: Israel’s newly elected parliament is already moving against Netanyahu
articles.content_orig:
The parliamentary bloc led by Israeli ex-military leader Gadi Eisenkot announced a slew of initiatives on Tuesday targeting the legacy of current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as the new Israeli Parliament, or Knesset, was sworn in.
Israel held a parliamentary election on October 27.
Eisenkot's centrist Yashar Party and allied parties are seeking an official government inquiry into the Hamas-led terror attacks on October 7, 2023, which killed some 1,200 people in Israel and resulted in another 251 hostages being taken into Gaza .
The attack, which occurred on Netanyahu's watch, was the single deadliest day for Jewish people since the Holocaust.
Some media outlets had reported that Netanyahu received warnings from Egypt and the UAE ahead of the October 7 assault. The Israeli prime minister denied the claims and said he would sue for defamation over the publications.
In addition to an October 7 probe, the anti-Netanyahu opposition is also seeking to impose term limits on the office of prime minister and aims to reverse the controversial efforts made by the Netanyahu government to reforming the judiciary .  Eisenkot's bloc is also seeking to depose Knesset speaker Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally.
"We will act for all citizens of Israel, those who voted for us and those who did not, out of deep commitment," Eisenkot said prior to the swearing-in of the new Knesset. He pledged to "form a national-emergency government as quickly as possible."
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has given Eisenkot a mandate to try to form a government within six weeks.
Eisenkot's coalition bloc landed 48 seats in the recent election, whereas Netanyahu's bloc received 53 seats. But neither bloc has enough seats to form a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.
Arab parties garnered a record 19 out of 120 seats in the new Knesset. During the swearing-in ceremony, far-right Israeli politician Itamar Ben-Gvir harassed Arab-Israeli lawmaker Yousef Jabareen in the Knesset chamber
Eisenkot's bloc could choose to align with the Arab parties to form a government, but Avigdor Lieberman and his right-wing Yisrael Beitenu party oppose the idea. Yisrael Beitenu, which won seven seats in the new Knesset, is a part of the Eisenkot bloc.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Netanyahu , in a speech to the Knesset, called for a national unity government — a proposal which has been ruled out by Eisenkot. The incumbent head of government lashed out at Arab parties and accused them of backing Israel's destruction while saying the national unity government is necessary to confront Iran .
"In the very near future, we're going to be confronted by international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran and the preservation of this terror regime that seeks to annihilate us," Netanyahu said.
Eisenkot condemned Netanyahu's remarks, whereas Yair Golan, the leader of the left-wing Democrats party, walked out during Netanyahu's speech. The Democrats have eight seats and are part of the Eisenkot bloc.
"Netanyahu is struggling to accept that the Israeli public fired him. Now he is lying and inciting against the Arab public in an attempt to cling to power by force," Golan said on X.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
If Eisenkot fails to form a government, Israeli President Herzog could choose another lawmaker, presumably Netanyahu, to cobble together a coalition. The 77-year-old Netanyahu first took power in 1996 and has had three separate stints as the Israeli head of government.
Netanyahu is now the longest-serving prime minister in Israeli history.

articles.title_orig: Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang, leaving 20 dead
articles.title_zh: Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang, leaving 20 dead
articles.content_orig:
El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele said that Salvadoran troops have targeted one of Haiti’s largest criminal organisations. It comes amid international calls to respect international human rights law.
Bukele announced the attack on Tuesday on the social media platform X.
“We destroyed the house of [gang leader] Lanmo San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang’s headquarters,” the right-wing leader wrote.
Bukele posted a video of helicopters circling overhead and firing on the site in Croix-des-Bouquets, near Port-au-Prince.
The operation was reportedly conducted on Sunday by Haitian police with support from Salvadoran troops, and resulted in the killing of 20 people.
The announcement comes as Haiti’s prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aime, prepares to visit El Salvador next week to discuss the future of Salvadoran troops in his gang-plagued Caribbean nation.
Amnesty International has urged both countries to ensure that all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law, and called on them to release the agreement governing the mass deployment.
“Both governments must make public the agreement governing the deployment and explain how they oversee the deployed forces, what rules govern the use of force, to whom they are accountable, and how people can report possible violations without fear of reprisals,” Amnesty’s Americas director Ana Piquer said.
“Ensure that all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law,” she urged the leaders of the two nations.
She also called on both countries to establish “prompt, independent and impartial investigations into all allegations of human rights violations”.
“The response to gang violence must not replicate the abuses and impunity that have characterized previous interventions in Haiti,” she added.
Some 2,000 troops have been sent by El Salvador’s president to Haiti since the mid-October disappearance of four Salvadoran personnel.
The vast majority are not participating in the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) , raising concerns about their rules of engagement.
Bukele initially stated the deployment aimed at bringing home four Salvadoran GSF soldiers who went missing during an ambush attack on October 18.
But more recently, he has hinted at a broader goal of eliminating Haiti’s powerful gangs, as he did in his own country with a campaign pockmarked with allegations of human rights abuses.
Haiti is set to hold elections in July and October next year, marking its first ones in more than a decade.

articles.title_orig: Aviva Helfand, 74, OBM
articles.title_zh: Aviva Helfand, 74, OBM
articles.content_orig:
Aviva Helfand , a beloved member of the Long Beach, CA Jewish community, known for her memorable meals and warm hospitality, passed away on Erev Shabbos, Parshas Vayera, 19 Cheshvan 5787. Full Story
Aviva Helfand , a beloved member of the Long Beach, CA Jewish community, known for her memorable meals and warm hospitality, passed away on Erev Shabbos, Parshas Vayera, 19 Cheshvan 5787. Full Story
Aviva Helfand , a beloved member of the Long Beach, CA Jewish community, known for her memorable meals and warm hospitality, passed away on Friday, Erev Shabbos Parshas Vayera, 19 Cheshvan 5787.
Legendary for her warm hospitality and delicious food, Aviva ran the kitchen at the Hebrew Academy of Huntington Beach and Camp Silver Gan Israel. She fed and cared for generations of students, teachers, campers and counselors with love and dedication.
Her passion for cooking and serving the community knew no bounds. As one of the few kosher caterers south of LA at the time, she curated beautiful events, cooked and baked for countless families and communities throughout Long Beach and Orange County. Her elegant cakes were often the centerpiece of simchas, renowned for tasting as good as they looked.
Born and raised in Los Angeles, Aviva’s early connection to Judaism took shape while living with her grandparents. Her grandfather, Carl Urstein (formerly Orenshtein), was the distinguished cantor of Sinai Temple. Aviva loved listening to him daven at the amud with passion and grace.
A free spirit with a colorful personality, Aviva adopted the hippie life and even briefly lived in a cave in the Big Sur mountains. She later worked alongside her mother, Judy, at her celebrated clothing shop on Hollywood’s Sunset Strip. The boutique attracted celebrities and rock stars, from Janis Joplin to Barbra Streisand.
Aviva’s journey took a turn in the 80s when she sent her son, Josh, to the Hebrew Academy (located in Long Beach at the time). Volunteering at their weekly Bingo fundraisers, Aviva made friends with Robin Greenspan, Sora Warhaftig and Angie Levin—friendships that would last a lifetime.
Through those connections, Aviva gradually returned to her family’s roots and embraced a life of Torah, Mitzvos and Chassidus (Aviva’s great-grandparents were Chassidim of the Frierdiker Rebbe in Eretz Yisroel).
After moving to Crown Heights, Aviva met her husband, Mottie Helfand , at the Shabbos table of the Hershkowitz family. Mottie had also made his own journey from being raised on Broadway to becoming a Chossid. Together, they returned to Long Beach and built a home known for its warmth, generosity, and hospitality.
A devoted mother, Aviva gave tirelessly to the community while caring for her daughter Mindy, who was born with special needs. She cared for Mindy with extraordinary love and dedication until her passing at nine and a half years old in September 2000.
Like Avraham Avinu’s tent, Aviva’s home was always open—a fitting connection to Parshas Vayera, the week of her passing. Her Shabbos and Yom Tov tables regularly welcomed dozens of guests. She kept china for 40, always ready for whoever might walk through her door. The Helfand home provided delicious meals and a place where everyone felt welcomed, cared for, and part of the family.
Shiva took place during the week of Parshas Chayei Sarah, which recounts Sarah Imeinu’s passing and the continuation of her legacy. Aviva, too, leaves a lasting legacy. The warmth, generosity, and love Aviva shared so freely continues to live on through her family and all those fortunate enough to have known her. Aviva will forever hold a cherished place in the annals of the Long Beach Chabad community.
She was predeceased by her husband, Mottie Helfand, in 5770; her daughter, Mindy, in September 2000; and her son, Joshua Hofer , in 5785.
She is survived by her children, Yosef Helfand and Esther Nolan , and their families, all of Long Beach, California; her sister, Nili Hudson , of Mar Vista, California; her grandchildren; and many others that were like family to her.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic opens Australian retail IPO offering as AI scrutiny intensifies
articles.title_zh: Anthropic opens Australian retail IPO offering as AI scrutiny intensifies
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic , the maker of AI chatbot Claude, opened its Australian retail initial public offering on Wednesday, giving individual investors access to shares ahead of the company's planned Nasdaq listing.
The offering opened at 10 a.m. Australian Eastern Daylight Time on Wednesday and is expected to close at 5 p.m. on Nov. 17, according to the timetable published by participating broker Stake.
Anthropic is seeking to raise as much as $64.4 billion in its IPO, with a separate $26 billion private placement, bringing a combined total to as much as $90.4 billion. Shares are expected to be priced between $70 to $78 each.
The Australian retail offering is expected to consist of newly issued Class A common shares under a prospectus to be lodged with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, Anthropic said on its website .
Participating brokers include Commonwealth Bank of Australia's CommSec unit as lead broker, along with Bell Potter, LGT Wealth, Macquarie Group, Morgans, Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, Sharesies and Stake.
Anthropic said the prospectus would be available on its IPO website once the Australian retail offering opens. Investors will need to review the document and apply through participating brokers under the terms of the offer.
Australia is one of the small numbers of markets outside the U.S. where retail investors will be able to buy the company's shares directly, alongside Japan, Canada and parts of Europe.
The San Francisco-based AI startup has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "ANT." Anthropic said it does not plan to seek a listing on the Australian Securities Exchange.
The offering comes as Australia moves to tighten oversight of AI companies after an OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to the medical statistics website of Medicare,  the country's universal health insurance program.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday that the government would introduce mandatory reporting for certain AI-related incidents and establish an AI safety regulator with powers to enforce penalties.
"The law needs to get ahead of, and in some cases, make sure that it catches up with what is a very fast-changing world," Albanese told Reuters.
The government is also considering changes to criminal law for cases involving serious misconduct.
The country has also ruled out a copyright-law exemption that would allow AI companies to train models on Australian content without licensing it.
Open AI and Anthropic told Australian parliament last month that they would support mandatory reporting of data breaches involving their AI agents, acknowledging that disclosure is currently voluntary.

articles.title_orig: Pentagon chief Hegseth defiant as US House blocks impeachment effort
articles.title_zh: Pentagon chief Hegseth defiant as US House blocks impeachment effort
articles.content_orig:
Lawmakers vote 211–204 to effectively shelve resolution after the US defence secretary mounts a fiery defence of the Iran war
US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth called an impeachment bid against him a “farce” on Tuesday, defending the ongoing war in Iran and the air strikes against drug traffickers as a “lawful operation”, just hours before the US House voted to approve a procedural motion to refer the resolution to a committee, effectively preventing his ousting.
He stressed that no US secretary of defence has ever been impeached for carrying out “lawful” and “successful” military operations. He predicted the effort would fail, invoking Trump’s two impeachments, both of which ended in Senate acquittals.

articles.title_orig: Scoop: Commerce Department received national security warning on Nvidia CEO affair
articles.title_zh: Scoop: Commerce Department received national security warning on Nvidia CEO affair
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang walked into the chipmaker's Santa Clara, California, headquarters on Monday and conducted his regular morning meeting with top-level executives, people familiar with the meeting told CNBC.
On Sunday, Huang had disclosed an extramarital affair to employees .
Huang kicked off the closed-door gathering by addressing his infidelity and sharing how sorry he was to his staff, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. They said Huang didn't take any questions and quickly pivoted to business and top agenda items of the day.
The CEO was also in the office on Tuesday, conducting meetings just one week ahead of the company's quarterly earnings report.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
People inside the artificial intelligence chip giant said Huang tried to project "business as usual," even as the probe moved forward into his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The CEO was in a romantic relationship with Alice Huang , a former Megaspeed executive, according to The Financial Times .
Sentiment toward Jensen Huang shifted on Sunday after the 63-year-old revealed in an email to employees that he had an affair, though he did not disclose with whom he had the relationship.
"I know an apology cannot undo what I have done," he wrote. "I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust." Nvidia's board opened an investigation and hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the probe on Tuesday.
Employees inside the firm described the mood to CNBC as "sad." One employee told CNBC that they were shocked by Jensen Huang's revelations.
People also told CNBC that longtime employees viewed Jensen Huang as an idol who could do no wrong and thought of him as a guiding light. Many employees at the company are also struggling to come to grips with the CEO's actions, the people said.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 to build graphics processing units for video game graphics. In recent years, the company has become synonymous with the AI boom, powering the technology that underpins large language models and the massive data center buildout.
A central figure in the development of every AI layer, the Nvidia CEO is also a key voice in Washington, even accompanying President Donald Trump on his trip to China in May . In September, Jensen Huang and his wife were pictured at the same table as Chinese President Xi Jinping for the White House's state dinner.
The news of the CEO's affair has drawn increased scrutiny on his continued support for more AI chip sales to China.

articles.title_orig: Fed’s Goolsbee Says October CPI Report ‘Borderline Disturbing’
articles.title_zh: Fed’s Goolsbee Says October CPI Report ‘Borderline Disturbing’
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Federal Reserve officials are monitoring the strength of demand in the US economy as they consider how high interest rates need to go to tame inflation.
Despite expected moratoriums on data centers in several states, Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee said Monday that the AI build-out is starting to look like more than just "old-fashioned demand overheating," noting that, anecdotally, everyone is trying to hire an electrician at the same time, which could cause prices to go up.
"The danger with that is nobody ever was under the impression that [inflation] just goes away on its own," Goolsbee said during a Q&A at the Chicago Fed. "If you get the economy overheated, the conventional wisdom is be aggressive up front to never let the economy overheat because once it gets overheated, it's extremely painful to get rid of that kind of overheating. So I think we got to watch out in that space."
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
Richmond Fed president Tom Barkin was a little more cautious, saying Monday that while inflation remains stubborn, there are risks to the durability of demand in the economy and that the Fed needs to move cautiously as it raises rates to tame inflation, so as not to knock the economy off course.
"With demand healthy and inflation stubbornly elevated, the appropriate direction of monetary policy is relatively straightforward," Barkin said in a speech in South Carolina. "However, risks to the demand outlook remain easy to envision. Because of that, it is wise to move policy with care."
Barkin noted that strong corporate earnings have been driven by explosive growth in the tech sector and strong demand, which has boosted profits for companies that had planned conservatively. Not to mention that GDP grew at 3.4% in the third quarter and productivity grew at 3.6% while wages have remained subdued.
However, Barkin said he wonders how long this earnings strength can last, noting that he's hearing widespread reports of broad-based cost pressures across health insurance, gas and diesel prices, trucking and ocean freight, memory chips, interest rates, and tariffs.
"The question is how businesses will react to margin pressure as we move into next year," Barkin said. "Will they find new avenues for growth? Scale back headcount and investment? Or find a way to recover these costs by raising their prices further?"
Barkin added that there's a question about the durability of consumer strength as well, noting that even as real incomes have flattened, consumers have found ways to keep spending. He said consumers are trading down to private labels and discount retailers, moving from beef to cheaper proteins, or turning to local food banks to supplement groceries. They're also making trade-offs by buying used items instead of new ones and choosing to repair rather than replace.
Still, Barkin said, inflation remains stubbornly elevated.
"Resilient demand paired with broad-based cost increases have put upward pressure on prices," he said. "Firms tell us this pressure continues and is leading them to also try to pass on increases that they've absorbed to date. Should the economy remain on its current path, the risk lies on the inflation side of our dual mandate."

articles.title_orig: 4 Bears Captured, Killed After Deadly Attack in Canada
articles.title_zh: 4 Bears Captured, Killed After Deadly Attack in Canada
articles.content_orig:
Canadian wildlife officials say four grizzly bears captured in western Canada were responsible for killing a mother and her adult daughter earlier this month in what investigators believe was a rare predatory attack
VANCOUVER, British Columbia -- Four grizzly bears captured in western Canada were responsible for killing a mother and her adult daughter this month in what investigators believe was a rare predatory attack, wildlife officials said Tuesday.
DNA tests conclusively linked a female grizzly and her three yearling cubs to the deaths of Jenny Balcarras, 48, and her 20-year-old daughter, Selah Reed, the British Columbia Conservation Officer Service said. All four bears were killed to protect the public.
“Our investigation also found that this attack likely involved predatory behavior, which I can tell you is very rare,” Inspector Jeff Tyre told an online briefing.
“That is to say, we don’t know how it started, but we know how it ended.”
The women’s remains were found about 150 meters (490 feet) apart near a trail outside Bella Coola, a remote community about 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) north of Vancouver.
Family members raised the alarm after Reed missed a routine Saturday night call with her sister. Searchers found her mother’s remains first, then discovered Reed’s remains in a bear cache, where bears store food.
Tyre said the bears were not involved in a separate grizzly attack last November on a group of about 20 elementary school students and teachers in the same area. Eleven people were injured, including two critically.
The latest killings have shaken the Nuxalk Nation community, which is still recovering from last year’s attack. Local authorities imposed a voluntary curfew, and police escorted children to school.
“This attack has been deeply re-triggering for our community members as we continue to recover from last year’s attack,” said Tlhmtimut Samuel Schooner, the Nuxalk Nation’s elected chief councilor.
He said community support services would remain available as long as needed.
Tyre said bears involved in fatal attacks cannot be rehabilitated or relocated because they pose an extreme risk to public safety.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft’s DLSS competitor is out for the Xbox Ally X and works in handheld mode
articles.title_zh: Microsoft’s DLSS competitor is out for the Xbox Ally X and works in handheld mode
articles.content_orig:
With the official launch of Auto SR, your Xbox Ally X can use Microsoft’s upscaling technology undocked and with games running at 1080p.
With the official launch of Auto SR, your Xbox Ally X can use Microsoft’s upscaling technology undocked and with games running at 1080p.
Microsoft is now rolling out Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR), an upscaling technology that competes with Nvidia’s DLSS, for the Xbox Ally X, Xbox Ally X20, and select Windows Copilot Plus PCs, the company announced today . Auto SR is also getting some new features alongside this official release.
In April, Microsoft started testing Auto SR on the Xbox Ally X, but you could only use it while docked. The full release of Auto SR announced today now works while you’re playing handheld and running on battery, and it also supports games running at 1080p. Microsoft does note that playing in handheld and at 1080p might lead to performance that “may not be as optimal as other configurations,” but says you’ll see visual improvements “especially in older games.”
Previously, Auto SR was also limited to framerates of “around” 60 to 75fps, but support for a new Auto SR Performance mode will allow you to hit framerates of up to 120fps. The Performance mode, and new compatibility with Auto HDR, will be available through Windows updates.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic bankers prepare to increase IPO valuation to $1.5tn or more
articles.title_zh: Anthropic bankers prepare to increase IPO valuation to $1.5tn or more
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic said it will offer 825 million shares in its upcoming IPO at a price range between $70 and $78 per share, according to an updated filing on Tuesday, bringing the 5-year-old artificial intelligence lab a step closer to a potentially historic Nasdaq debut.
The company is planning to price on Nov. 18 and trade on Nov. 19, according to people familiar with the details who were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly. Anthropic is targeting retail allocation of about 20%, the people said, a much higher percentage than the typical initial public offering, which is 5% to 10% for retail investors.
At the high end of the range, Anthropic would net up to $64.35 billion in proceeds through the IPO. The company could end up being worth up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, rising from the $965 billion valuation it announced as part of a funding round in May.
Anthropic said it has entered into an agreement with Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Google , Micron , Microsoft , Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to purchase $26 billion of the company's Class N common stock in a private placement at a price per share equal to the IPO price. The shares sold in the private placement will not be registered in the offering and will not be subject to lock-up agreements with the underwriters, the company said.
As Anthropic executives get set to pitch the offering to investors, they have to contend with a tumultuous political environment , following last week's midterm elections that included a Democratic sweep in Congress and the passage of numerous statewide ballot measures that could slow the AI buildout. They're also facing a public market that's grown increasingly skeptical of the AI trade on concern that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for companies that need it for costly infrastructure purchases.
CNBC reported last week that some Anthropic investors were bracing for a lower valuation than had previously been expected. While Anthropic had been looking toward a $2 trillion valuation until recently, shareholders told CNBC that even $1.5 trillion is now in doubt, with one investor calling that number a "stretch."
Should Anthropic reach the Nasdaq this month as planned, under the ticker symbol "ANT," the debut would come roughly five months after SpaceX went public in a record offering that raised $85.7 billion. Elon Musk's reusable rocket and AI company has a market cap of just under $2 trillion, around its valuation at the time of the IPO.
Institutional demand for Anthropic is even stronger than it was for SpaceX at this point in the process, the people said. The company's book is already covered at the $70 to $78 per share range on an allocable basis, they said.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the AI lab in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, and the company primarily sells its products and services to other businesses.
On Monday, Anthropic introduced two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, the first time the company has released so-called frontier models since Amodei called to slow down the pace of AI development in September . Anthropic said that the models went through rigorous safety and alignment testing, and that the company developed new evaluations and post-launch monitoring tools ahead of the release.
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said.
Anthropic said in its amended filing Tuesday that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month.
"Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort. We hope you will share our ambition to see it though."

articles.title_orig: Will China’s maritime moves push Japan and South Korea closer together?
articles.title_zh: Will China’s maritime moves push Japan and South Korea closer together?
articles.content_orig:
A sharp rise in naval transits could give Tokyo and Seoul good reason to put historical rancour aside, analysts say
A reported sharp increase in Chinese warships and coastguard vessels passing through the strait that separates the two countries, some operating alongside Russian forces, has raised concerns about Beijing’s expanding maritime reach.

articles.title_orig: Latvia, Lithuania warn of new drone threats as Finland adopts curbs
articles.title_zh: Latvia, Lithuania warn of new drone threats as Finland adopts curbs
articles.content_orig:
Following the failure to shoot down one of the drones that entered Latvian airspace last week, procedures have been reviewed and the decision-making chain shortened to enable faster responses in the future, Defence Minister Raivis Melnis said on Monday during an interview with Latvian Television's Rīta panorāma programme.
The minister explained that drone interception teams operating on the ground will now have greater decision-making authority, allowing them to act when they detect a target.
Meanwhile, the command centre will be able to suspend an interception mission if allied aircraft enter the threat area and their safety could be compromised.
Melnis said he had personally reviewed the entire decision-making process together with military commanders in Latvia's eastern border region, removing some of the additional safeguards that had previously been introduced.
Explaining the previous failure, the minister acknowledged that the drone had been detected and was being followed by an interceptor drone. However, due to existing procedures and possibly a lack of experience, the target was not destroyed.
Melnis apologised to residents for the failure.
The minister explained that Latvia had previously also relied on allied aircraft for drone interception.
When an interceptor drone and allied aircraft are operating in the same airspace, additional coordination is required to ensure that attempts to destroy the drone do not endanger other aircraft.
According to the minister, additional radar systems have been deployed along Latvia's eastern border to detect drones earlier and enable a more timely response.
The drone interception system was deployed at the end of September, as previously promised, and military personnel are continuing to learn how to operate it.
Melnis emphasised that the system's ability to detect a drone and launch an interceptor drone had been successfully tested in practice.
Last week, Latvian entrepreneurs also worked alongside soldiers in the border region to improve the system.
The minister expressed hope that aligning operational procedures with technical solutions would enable successful drone interceptions in the future.
The State Police reported receiving information on Saturday morning about suspected drone debris found in a forest in Liepna Parish.
Upon arriving at the scene and examining the difficult-to-access forest area, officers confirmed the report.
The State Police completed their work at the scene on Saturday evening, although investigative activities will continue.
Criminal proceedings have been initiated under Chapter 10 of the Criminal Law, "Crimes Against the State".
The National Armed Forces (NBS) have also launched an internal investigation to assess the circumstances of the incident and the decisions made.
According to the NBS, information was received on the 18th of October about an explosion-like sound in Liepna Parish, Alūksne Municipality.
After receiving the report from the State Police, the NBS began an in-depth analysis of data from airspace surveillance systems.
The analysis revealed information suggesting that an unidentified object may have travelled through Latvian airspace.
Based on these findings, the NBS, in cooperation with the State Police, launched a search for the object's possible crash site.
Search operations continued on the 19th of October.
However, after two days, the search was suspended because the information available at the time was insufficient to confirm that the object had crashed or to determine its possible location.

articles.title_orig: Fortis Games closes down, affecting 440 jobs | exclusive
articles.title_zh: Fortis Games closes down, affecting 440 jobs | exclusive
articles.content_orig:
Fortis Games , an ambitious game publisher with a lot of financial back, is closing down and could be shedding as many as 440 jobs, GamesBeat has learned.
The San Francisco-based game company acquired multiple studios and grew over time. It was headed by an all-star team including Steven Chiang, CEO, and the former executive vice president of worldwide studios for WB Games. He was also a longtime EA Sports exec and also worked at Zynga as a game leader.
The initial money came from Las Vegas Sands, a company started by Sheldon Adelson (now deceased) and known as the creator of the Venetian Hotel on the Las Vegas Strip.
On LinkedIn, various Fortis employees said they had been laid off and some said the company is shutting down.
In a statement to GamesBeat, Chiang said, “Fortis has been a labor of love for so many of us and we’re disappointed we weren’t able to achieve the goals we set for ourselves when we started this journey more than five years ago. We have been fortunate to work with some of the most talented and dedicated people in this space. As we move forward, our primary focus will be on helping this talented team of individuals find new opportunities. Thank you to everyone who has supported us over the past five years. We are grateful for the collaboration and friendship we have shared with so many.”
Pedro Gomes, concept artist at Fortis Games, wrote on LinkedIn , “Today marks the end of my journey at Fortis Games, as the company has officially shut down. Over the past five years, I’ve had the privilege of collaborating with truly exceptional people. I am incredibly grateful for everything we’ve built, learned, and created together. Being part of such a talented team has been an amazing experience, and I truly hope our paths cross again.”
And Scott Butterworth, communications director, wrote on LinkedIn, “ Fortis Games — what could have been. Despite our unique, community-focused approach to the mobile games  market, we just couldn’t seem to get off the ground, and today, we finally ran out of runway. The company has officially shuttered, abruptly putting more than 400 talented people out of work (myself included).”
And Gustavo Coronet, an employee in game production at Fortis, wrote on LinkedIn , Today Fortis Games has been abruptly shut down.
“Las Vegas Sands has chosen to end funding and part ways, terminating all of the contracts, worldwide,” Coronet said. “Super proud of the work we’ve done. LVS’s decision does not delete the groundbreaking and best-in class agentic development workflow the Octopus team has built, nor the massively solid soft launch metrics both our project were achieving in such early stages of development.”
Among the companies Fortis acquired were three development teams: Doppio Games, in Portugal; Oktagon Games in Brazil, and Metagame in Romania. The ambition, as related by Patrick Dumont, Las Vegas Sands president in 2022, was to move into the interactive entertainment medium as a core pillar for diversifying beyond gambling. Dumont said the company was assembling a team to build games from the ground up.
The core leadership for the developer and publisher came from executives from Electronic Arts, WB Games, Zynga, Smule and more.
Fortis initially focused on creating the next generation of the video games as service model, pushing forward game design and social mechanics to enable digital societies and enduring group experiences that foster relationships and memories.
The founders believed online social experiences could be more positive and meaningful, and that games could become the primary form of social entertainment. Chiang happened to be a judge of our Mobile Mogul Awards contest for best mobile gaming execs, and he appeared on a panel about that at our recent GamesBeat Next 2026 event.
Chiang rose through the ranks at EA Sports at EA. He left Electronic Arts and went to Zynga in 2010 on the basis of his belief in games-as-a-service and free-to-play as the business model of the future that could attract broad markets. The expectation at Fortis was that Las Vegas Sands would be a long-term investor.
Fortis also announced that it was shutting down its game Twilight Towers on November 16.
In that announcement, Fortis said, “Over the past several months, our team has worked hard to improve Twilight Towers: introducing new features, redesigning major systems, and trying different approaches to make the game more engaging. We asked you to endure a lot along the way, including progress resets and map changes. Your willingness to keep coming back and to share your feedback meant a great deal to us.”
And Fortis added, “Ultimately, though, keeping a live game running takes ongoing investment in development, content, servers, and player support, and despite our best efforts, we just weren’t seeing strong enough player retention to make the game sustainable. This is not a reflection of the players who supported us. We’re grateful for the community that grew around this game; the responsibility for this outcome is ours.”

articles.title_orig: Girl, 5, shoots and kills little sister, 3, after dad left loaded gun on kitchen counter
articles.title_zh: Girl, 5, shoots and kills little sister, 3, after dad left loaded gun on kitchen counter
articles.content_orig:
A five-year-old girl fatally shot her little sister after their father reportedly left his loaded gun on the kitchen counter before he headed to bed.
Olivia Melo Moreira, 3, was found dead by her parents Sunday morning on the floor of their Rio de Janeiro home — as her stunned sister ran toward them repeatedly saying “Sorry, Daddy,” the devastated father told police, according to The Sun .
Moreira was rushed to a local hospital where she succumbed to her injuries, O Globo reported .
The dad, a licensed gun owner who has not yet been identified, was interviewed by police.
He was not immediately arrested but is expected to be charged with involuntary manslaughter and failure to exercise proper caution with a firearm, according to The Sun.
“At this very delicate and tragic moment, the family has no interest whatsoever in making a statement,” the dad’s attorney told reporters.
The little girl’s family had been out late for a street party that went on until 6 a.m. Sunday morning. When they returned to the house, Moreira’s mother noticed the garage gate was wide open and alerted her husband, who took his pistol downstairs to check whether anyone had broken in.
He found no burglars and went back to bed — but tragically left the loaded pistol, still in its holster, on the kitchen counter.
A loud bang awoke the parents who discovered their daughter on the floor.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
The father had registered the weapon as a licensed sports shooter and hunter.
Police have seized the gun and the investigation remains ongoing.

articles.title_orig: Seagate’s new hybrid drive raises some old questions
articles.title_zh: Seagate’s new hybrid drive raises some old questions
articles.content_orig:
Seagate doesn’t think hybrid drives are done just yet. On Tuesday, the company announced the launch of the new FireCuda Forge line of storage drives. The new drives combine the high capacity of a traditional plattered HDD with the speed and responsiveness of a user-supplied solid-state drive (SSD). The new hybrid storage solution is Seagate’s first to be powered and managed by the new Alkemi intelligent storage platform.
The FireCuda Forge is available right now through Seagate’s web store , and comes in 8TB ($699) or 20TB ($899) HDD configurations—neither of which includes the required SSD. Users will have to bring their own SSD, with some specific restrictions. The FireCuda Forge is compatible with M.2 2280 NVMe drives that are PCIe Gen3 or higher. The maximum supported NVMe capacity is 1TB, which means that’s as much data as you’ll be able to dedicate to storage on the “fast side” of the hybrid setup. The NVMe will require minimum speeds of 2,400MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write, and a unit with DRAM cache is recommended. Seagate claims 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write speeds for the combined system, along with USB4 and support for Windows 11 and macOS 26+.
Credit: Seagate Credit: Seagate
After dipping to historical lows earlier in the decade, storage pricing per TB has exploded amid the AI boom. According to data collected by Tom’s Hardware , some solid-state drives now cost two to three times their historic lows, and it’s not just SSDs. Mechanical drives haven’t been immune either. According to PCServerParts , a Seagate Exos 24TB drive that sold for $298.99 in the summer of 2025 was priced at $699.99 by August 2026.
Hybrid drives had largely fallen out of fashion since their heyday in the early to mid 2010s. The promise then was similar to what Seagate is offering now. A large HDD is combined with a smaller SSD and handed to the user as a single storage pool. Apple introduced its own hybrid solution back in 2012 with the Mac mini’s Fusion Drive. When Ars opened up a unit , the Fusion Drive system was found to write in 128KB tiered blocks. Information was generally written to the SSD first, and was then migrated to the HDD as needed. If the files were frequently used, they might find a more permanent home on the SSD side of things.
As solid-state storage continued getting cheaper, the hybrid approach was largely abandoned. Fast-forward to our current storage cost predicament in 2026, and Seagate’s line of thinking that everything old is new again starts to hold water. All storage costs have exploded, but the 2012 math still works today. NAND flash is still fast, but expensive, and traditional mechanical drives are at least comparatively cheaper per TB for higher capacity storage.
The problem with Apple’s Fusion solution was its fragility. If one of the two drives failed, that was likely it. Recovery depended on both drives coming together as a single volume. If one of those two disks experienced a physical failure, recovery became difficult since the remaining working drive depended on the now broken drive’s data to rebuild the full system picture.
According to Seagate’s press release, the Alkemi intelligent storage platform takes a different approach. Where Apple’s Fusion Drives used tiering managed by macOS, Alkemi manages the storage pool directly from the enclosure. Seagate says, “ Alkemi learns and adapts over time to keep high-demand content fast and accessible on a user’s SSD, while the HDD provides space for growing libraries. Behind the scenes, Alkemi manages data placement, giving users the simplicity of a single storage drive. ” The product data sheet PDF from the FireCuda Forge website describes the Alkemi system as a two-tier storage system, but doesn’t elaborate any further on whether the system uses SSD caching, automated tiering, a combination of the two, or something else entirely.
The announcement doesn’t address how the Alkemi platform manages the data between the two drives. The old Intel Smart Response Technology kept failure risks low by mirroring data from the mechanical HDD to the faster SSD, with the HDD retaining the authoritative copy. The optional write-back mode could still hold new data on the SSD, though. Apple’s Fusion Drive instead tiered data in 128KB blocks across the storage pool, storing data on both drives. The distinction matters, and is probably why Ars asked the same question after Apple’s hybrid announcement 14 years ago.
Seagate’s announcement speaks of “ intelligent data tiering ” without further explanation. The data system promises that your most accessed files will be quickest to access via intelligent storage management, but stops short of explaining whether one drive going down means failure for the whole system. There’s also no mention of how the Alkemi system distributes data on first boot. Does all the new written data go directly to the SSD until the 1TB cap is crossed, and then the system starts determining which files are important enough to remain on the speedier drive? Seagate seems to be keeping things mum for the moment, but as the drives have already launched for sale, there should be answers to all of these questions coming soon.
Seagate hasn’t published technical documentation regarding how the Alkemi system handles drive failure or repair. Until it does, the new FireCuda Forge drives offer the same appeal as Apple’s old Fusion Drives: SSD speed with HDD capacity, along with the same questions Ars was asking about hybrid storage years ago .

articles.title_orig: China’s Space Station Cools Atoms to a Record-Low 9.7 Trillionths of a Degree Above Absolute Zero
articles.title_zh: China’s Space Station Cools Atoms to a Record-Low 9.7 Trillionths of a Degree Above Absolute Zero
articles.content_orig:
By XANTHA LEATHAM, EXECUTIVE SCIENCE EDITOR
Published: 05:34 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 05:34 EST, 10 November 2026
Scientists aboard China 's Tiangong space station have chilled a cloud of atoms to just 9.7 picokelvin, the coldest temperature ever measured.
The record-breaking experiment took advantage of the station's microgravity environment, allowing researchers to study matter at temperatures closer to absolute zero than ever before.
The atoms were chilled to just 9.7 trillionths of a degree above absolute zero, around 280 billion times colder than the average temperature of the Universe.
The feat smashes the previous record of 38 picokelvin, which was achieved in a microgravity experiment on Earth in 2021.
Researchers say the breakthrough opens a new frontier in the quest to understand the strangest laws of quantum physics.
‘This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of…experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space,’ the team, from Peking University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, wrote in the journal Science .
The experiment was carried out using the Cold Atom Physics Rack housed inside the Mengtian laboratory module of China's orbiting space station
Researchers calculated the record-breaking temperature by tracking the slow expansion of an ultracold cloud of atoms, which remained visible for seven seconds after being released
The experiment was carried out using the Cold Atom Physics Rack housed inside the Mengtian laboratory module of China's orbiting space station.
The weightless environment of space was crucial because gravity on Earth makes it harder to keep ultracold atoms stable for long periods.
Inside the facility, scientists trapped about 20,000 rubidium atoms and cooled them until they formed an exotic state of matter known as a Bose-Einstein condensate.
This bizarre state occurs when atoms become so cold that they begin behaving like a single giant quantum object.
To push temperatures even lower, the team transferred the atoms into a trap made of laser light and allowed them to expand under carefully controlled conditions.
The researchers were able to observe the freezing cloud of atoms for an extraordinary seven seconds as it expanded freely.
Inside the facility, scientists trapped about 20,000 rubidium atoms and cooled them until they formed an exotic state of matter known as a Bose-Einstein condensate
This image illustrates atoms held in an optical trap aboard China's space station, where they were cooled to 10 picokelvin - the lowest temperature reached in space
While the temperatures involved are almost impossible to comprehend, they are still technically above absolute zero, the theoretical point at which all atomic motion ceases.
Scientists have pursued ever-lower temperatures for decades because ultracold atoms provide an ideal laboratory for testing fundamental physics.
Experiments at these temperatures could help researchers probe mysterious quantum states that cannot be studied under ordinary conditions.
The work may also pave the way for a new generation of ultra-sensitive atom interferometers capable of making exquisitely precise measurements.
Such instruments could one day be used to test Einstein's theory of gravity, hunt for new physics and even aid future gravitational-wave detection efforts.
The researchers say their all-optical cooling platform is particularly well suited to future space missions because it can be adapted for a wide range of experiments.

Neocloud player CoreWeave saw shares swing in extended trading Tuesday afternoon after beating expectations on revenue in the third quarter .
The company also raised its guidance for the full year. Shares were initially positive in after hours before dipping into negative territory.
The results come as shares of CoreWeave have been subject to selling pressure amid rising worries that the artificial intelligence data center build-out could see a slowdown. The company's bond yields have also been marching higher.
Follow below as CNBC breaks down the biggest stock market moves of the day.
Mercury Systems , the maker of aerospace and defense electronics and signal and data processing systems fell almost 3% postmarket after rising 5% in regular trading Tuesday.
Mercury earned 52 cents a share in its fiscal first quarter, above the 33-cent highest estimate among 13 analysts polled by FactSet. Revenue of $253.2 million similarly beat the highest estimate on the Street, at $246.2 million.
Mercury shares are ahead 14.5% so far in 2026.
Grocery Outlet fell 8% after the company posted mixed results for the third quarter. The grocery store chain's revenue came in at $1.18 billion for the period, just above a FactSet consensus of $1.17 billion. Adjusted earnings per share totaled 16 cents, in line with estimates.
NextNav , the ground-based backup for GPS, climbed 8% postmarket after falling 6% during the regular trading session Tuesday.
Third-quarter revenue nearly doubled from the same period a year ago, while the quarterly loss narrowed to 4 cents a share from 12 cents last year. Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments on hand rose to $264.1 million on Sept. 30 from $152.1 million on Dec. 31, the company said.
Based in Reston, Virginia, NextNav is down 50% in 2026 and has a market value of about $1.5 billion, according to FactSet data.
Shares climbed more than 9%.
CoreWeave shares traded 1% higher after the neocloud company reported third-quarter revenue that exceeded analyst expectations.
The company's top line came in at $3.66 billion, marking a 168% surge from the year-earlier period. Analysts polled by LSEG expected revenue of $3.55 billion. CoreWeave also hiked its full-year revenue outlook.
Rigetti Computing's third-quarter results disappointed the Street, sending shares down in after-hours trading.
The quantum computing stock was last down more than 6%.
Rigetti lost 8 cents per share, worse than the FactSet consensus estimate of a 5 cents per share loss. Revenue was well below expectations, landing at $1.4 million versus the consensus estimate of $3.5 million.
Full-year guidance also disappointed, with the company calling for roughly $20 million in revenue for the period, while the FactSet consensus sought $22.6 million.
The space company saw shares decline in extended trading after narrowing its full-year revenue guidance.
Firefly Aerospace sees revenue in a range of $440 million to $450 million, versus its earlier call for $420 million to $450 million. The FactSet consensus estimate sought $439.4 million.
Firefly's third-quarter report was better than expected, with the company reporting an adjusted loss of 45 cents a share on revenue of $110.7 million. Analysts polled by FactSet were looking for a loss of 50 cents a share and $102.3 million.
Microsoft shares dropped 3% in a sudden move after Anthropic announced a slate of new workplace tools for Claude that could compete with Office.
Anthropic introduced Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards and Claude Data in a blog post .
"Starting today, Claude can build spreadsheets, whiteboards, and dashboards with your team," the post said.
Shares of On Holding fell 8% as investors looked beyond a one-time tariff refund of 52.6 million Swiss francs and focused on a direct-to-consumer sales miss.
Adjusted earnings rose from a year earlier and topped the FactSet consensus estimate. Net income increased 36.9% to 162.8 million Swiss francs.
Net sales at the Swiss sportswear and athletic-footwear company rose 17.2% to 931.4 million Swiss francs, slightly above the FactSet consensus estimate of 930.3 million Swiss francs.
Broken down by segments, direct-to-consumer generated revenue of 393.3 million Swiss francs, falling short of the StreetAccount estimate for 417.7 million Swiss francs.
The company reported a gross margin of 72.6%, or 66.9% excluding the tariff refund.
Shares of the chip giant tumbled more than 6% on the day, touching $166.52 a share in midday trading.
Nvidia has been skidding to start the week as traders assess the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Shares of Trump Media & Technology Group climbed 7% after the company reported a profitable third quarter and a surge in revenue over the period.
The company posted net income of $409.7 million in the third quarter, which includes gains on digital assets, up from the year-ago loss of $54.8 million. Revenue came in at $3 million, up more than 200% from the year-ago period.
Companies tied to home construction tumbled after October's consumer inflation report came in hot and market expectations for a December rate hike climbed.
Fed funds futures now suggests a 100% likelihood of a rate increase in December. Such a move would influence the bond market and in turn rates on mortgages.
The iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF (ITB) fell more than 3%.
Homebuilders Lennar and D.R. Horton lost 5% and 4%, respectively, while Floor & Decor Holdings slid 3%.
Carlyle Group fell 1% after UBS downgraded the stock to neutral from buy, cutting its price target to $47 from its prior target of $60.
Analyst Michael Brown sees the risk/reward as balanced, noting that Carlyle's newer growth businesses are not yet large enough to offset its dependence on flagship fundraising. Carlyle is increasingly likely to miss its 2028 earnings, according to the analyst.
"We lowered our fee-related earnings multiple to 8 times and price-to-earnings multiple to 8 times in our 50/50 blended SoTP framework," Brown said. "This reflects an estimated 10.7% three-year CAGR in fee-related earnings from 2025 to 2028, reduced visibility into when flagship funds will begin generating fees and a less diversified growth strategy than faster-growing peers."
Data center power producer GE Vernova is sliding in Tuesday morning trading following revisions from SoftBank on its power equipment procurement strategy. Shares of GEV are down close to 7% as of 10:35 a.m. ET.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX plans $24 billion data center project in Starbase
articles.title_zh: SpaceX plans $24 billion data center project in Starbase
articles.content_orig:
About The Texas Tribune | Staff | Contact | Send a Confidential Tip | Ethics | Republish Our Work | Jobs | Awards | Corrections | Strategic Plan | Downloads | Documents
Our reporting on all platforms will be truthful, transparent and respectful; our facts will be accurate, complete and fairly presented. When we make a mistake — and from time to time, we will — we will work quickly to fully address the error, correcting it within the story, detailing the error on the story page and adding it to this running list of Tribune corrections. If you find an error, email corrections@texastribune.org .
Subscribe to The Y’all — a weekly dispatch about the people, places and policies defining Texas, produced by Texas Tribune journalists living in communities across the state.
McALLEN — SpaceX is planning to build a $24 billion data center and power plant just outside of Brownsville on property that the city had just de-annexed earlier this year at the company’s request, circumventing Brownsville’s data center moratorium that went into effect last week.
On Monday, the city of Starbase, which later annexed land where the project will be built into their city limits, notified the public that SpaceX is building a $24 billion “gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility.”
The $24 billion investment is expected to cover the initial phases of the project which could include future expansions, according to the Monday notice which stated that the Starbase city commissioners are scheduled to hold a public hearing in December in which they will consider tax breaks for the project.
The 444.45 acres of land where the project will be located was the subject of local scrutiny over the summer, when SpaceX asked the city of Brownsville to de-annex that land. In exchange, the company offered to fund $220 million for city water and wastewater projects.
A SpaceX representative didn’t provide details as to why the company wanted the land, located near the Port of Brownsville out of Brownsville’s city limits, but the company pressured the city to approve the de-annexation quickly or else the $220 million would be off the table. The city agreed, but the move drew widespread condemnation from residents and environmental activists who believed the city was allowing SpaceX to further take over land in the area.
Soon after the city approved the deal, speculation circulated online that SpaceX planned to build a data center on the property and wished to circumvent a data center moratorium that was advancing within Brownsville.
That speculation appears to have been correct all along.
In response to the news, the South Texas Environmental Justice Network, announced a protest against the project, arguing that the new facilities would pollute the air, use up water and increase energy bills for residents.
Other residents responded positively, seeing the project as a source for more jobs.
“There’s a lot of people that need jobs in our community and SpaceX has contributed to those jobs,” said Janie Melendez, a Brownsville resident and school teacher.
She previously served on the Texas Republican Party’s executive committee but said her politics don’t influence her view on data centers and SpaceX.
“Since SpaceX moved in, my home has tripled in value,” she said. “But I’m one of those [people] that tries to find a balance in everything.”
SpaceX did not respond to questions regarding the project.
However, a majority of Texans oppose data center construction, which has received a wave of pushback across the state due to concerns over how much power and water they require to operate at a time when utility bills remain high and water scarcity fears mount. In response to public backlash, several communities have issued temporary moratoriums on data centers.
As criticisms of these facilities grew, Gov. Greg Abbott directed operators of the electric grid in August to pause requests for data center connections to the grid until the data centers could be audited. However, not all data centers rely on the state’s power grid and therefore could still move forward by supplying their own electricity.
The gas-fired power plant that SpaceX plans to build could provide power to its data center to avoid connecting to the state’s power grid.
Abbott also ordered the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to stop issuing permits for data centers, though critics say that some permits have continued to advance through the permitting process.
Data center developers could face stronger headwinds under Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa , who said she would issue a ban on all data center approvals until state legislators can pass laws “to protect Texans,” she said in a video posted on X .
Brownsville approved its own 90-day moratorium which went into effect last week, temporarily hitting pause on data center applications within the city and its extraterritorial jurisdiction. Had the 444.45-acre tract of land remained within Brownsville’s city limits, the SpaceX project likely would have had to find a different location.
The city of Brownsville said it stood by its decision to de-annex the property, which was based on “information and circumstances presented at the time,” the city said in a statement. That included the property’s location, municipal service considerations and potential long-term benefits to Brownsville.
The city further noted that the land was privately owned and its sale to SpaceX was a transaction between private parties.
The $220 million that the city received for the de-annexation will fund critical water infrastructure which the city said would help ensure their water supply keeps up with their future growth.
“The City recognizes the concerns raised about data center development and takes those concerns seriously,” the city said. “It remains committed to evaluating those concerns and protecting water resources, evaluating infrastructure impacts and ensuring responsible growth that serves Brownsville’s long-term interests.”
Further, the city assured that any future de-annexation requests will be evaluated independently under state law and the city commission will take the circumstances and legal requirements into consideration before taking action.
“Residents should have confidence that their concerns about data center development, water resources, energy consumption and responsible growth are being taken seriously,” the city said. “Our responsibility is to ensure that Brownsville’s growth is intentional, that residents’ interests remain a priority, and that decisions involving our community’s future are made with transparency, accountability and careful consideration.”

articles.title_orig: Ring cameras go mobile as Amazon debuts AI-powered security drone and robot
articles.title_zh: Ring cameras go mobile as Amazon debuts AI-powered security drone and robot
articles.content_orig:
Amazon is betting that many Ring customers will also want an AI-powered security drone and robot patrolling their homes or offices. But the company’s upcoming Ring Robotic products are also certain to intensify privacy concerns previously raised around a prior Amazon attempt to popularize a flying security camera.
The Ring Rover Cam and Ring Drone Cam are expected to reach customers starting at the end of 2026 and in early 2027, respectively, according to an Amazon announcement posted on November 10. Amazon describes the devices as relying on an AI Pilot system that uses each device’s cameras along with “specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing” to plan patrol routes while autonomously navigating around obstacles such as furniture.
Both devices also use that AI Pilot system to digitally map the floor plan of the customer’s home or business. This setup process occurs after the customer carries the Ring drone through their indoor spaces or allows the Ring Rover to do some autonomous exploration.
The AI Pilot can supposedly use that guided- or self-tour information to identify specific rooms and suggest patrol points near side doors, windows, or even sensitive locations such as a cash register in the case of a business.
However, flying and roving cameras with AI-enabled features could introduce new privacy risks for homes and businesses, on top of existing concerns involving fixed Ring cameras installed in room corners or as doorbell cameras.
Amazon’s Ring Drone appears to be a direct successor to the company’s Ring Always Home Cam that was only temporarily available for purchase by invitation as a “Day 1 Edition” product in September 2021—even having the same starting price of $250.
But the Ring Drone still requires authorization from the Federal Communications Commission before going on sale. Assuming that comes through, Amazon aims to make the drone available on January 27, 2027, with customers able to register for email updates through the product page .
The drone can supposedly follow a set route and schedule for customers who subscribe to the Amazon Ring Protect plan. It can automatically fly along those set routes when responding to a notification from a Ring camera, sensor, or alarm.
Onboard camera capability includes a 148-degree field of view and 360-degree rotation with a 2K video resolution. Two LED lights also activate in low-light conditions to help illuminate the scene for the drone video camera.
However, the drone is limited to just 8 minutes of flight time when operating on a “new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions” according to the product description. It comes with a docking station for charging.
Another caveat in the product description is that the Ring Drone Cam may experience degraded performance when navigating in environments with reflective surfaces such as “polished marble or wet tile,” blank matte walls without any features, or transparent surfaces like frameless glass and mirrors.
Still, Amazon touts the drone as providing an “autonomous way to check on your home that has never existed before,” whether the customer is away or at home. The Ring Drone can be controlled directly from the Alexa Home Map interactive map that shows all of a customer’s Amazon-linked devices.
Meanwhile, Amazon has pitched the Ring Rover Cam priced at $1,000 as “an autonomous security robot designed for business.” This product is already available for preorder for those so inclined and scheduled to start shipping to customers on December 16, 2026.
The company described the Ring Rover as being inspired by customer feedback involving another invite-only beta product, the Amazon Astro robot designed for home monitoring.
The Ring Rover can livestream and record in up to 4K video resolution when patrolling or while doing a 360-degree scan at a designated location. Videos triggered by doorbell rings, motion events and “Live View” events are stored in the cloud for sharing and replaying for up to 180 days.
Like the Ring Drone, the Ring Rover can automatically respond to alerts from connected Ring devices by following its preprogrammed patrol points. But the wheeled robot is only designed to operate within a single-floor, indoor environment because it lacks stair-climbing capability.
Amazon’s product description also warns that the Rover is not compatible with “curved edges, sunken areas, flooring transitions greater than 1.375 inches (3.5 centimeters), and black glossy floors.”
To help compensate for its ground-based view, the Ring Rover comes with an automatically adjustable mast to peer over counters, shelving and other obstacles. It can supposedly cover up to 5,000 square feet (465 square meters), according to Amazon’s product description.
The Ring Rover also comes with additional security-related features such as a siren and light tower to loudly announce its presence, along with a microphone for two-way audio communication if the customer wants to address someone near the robot.
Amazon touts the new Ring Robotics products as offering “privacy and security without compromise,” with features such as LED indicators and screen notifications informing customers when video and audio recordings are active. But Ring, as an Amazon subsidiary, has been previously implicated in multiple privacy and security scandals.
Ring was previously charged in a 2023 Federal Trade Commission investigation with allowing employees and contractors to watch Ring video recordings of customers’ private spaces . The FTC also described Ring as having lackluster safeguards that allowed hackers to access 55,000 US customers’ accounts.
Videos taken by the new Ring Drone and Ring Rover will be protected with Ring’s Throw Away the Key Encryption that was introduced in September 2026, according to Amazon’s announcement. The digital rights nonprofit Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) has described this as an improvement over Ring’s former default settings, but still well short of end-to-end encryption.
The EFF has also called out what it describes as Ring founder Jamie Siminoff’s “surveillance-first-privacy-last” approach to Ring devices, including Ring reintroducing features that allow law enforcement to request footage or live-stream access from Ring users’ home security devices.
Amazon’s previous attempt to launch its Ring Always Home Cam drone also led to expanded privacy concerns. Ryan Calo , a law and technology researcher at the University of Washington, previously described such a flying security camera as providing new ways to surveil others indoors, along with giving companies much greater access to potentially sensitive or identifying details of homes and businesses.
There is currently no mention of the new Ring Robotics products implementing facial recognition or similar AI-powered technologies for identifying people. But starting in December 2025, Ring has allowed owners of fixed Ring doorbell cameras to turn on a “Familiar Faces” feature that uses facial recognition technology on visitors—and that is already the subject of a class action lawsuit .

articles.title_orig: Pentagon threatens to ‘physically’ remove reporters if they ‘get out of line’
articles.title_zh: Pentagon threatens to ‘physically’ remove reporters if they ‘get out of line’
articles.content_orig:
A security agent for Pete Hegseth threatened to physically remove reporters from his press conference if they did not âmaintain decorum,â marking the latest apparent attempt by the Pentagon to crack down on press freedom.
As Congress moves to potentially impeach Hegseth over the Iran war and other alleged abuses of power, the controversial defense secretary gave his first press conference in about six months on Tuesday to mount a furious defense of his record.
U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth gestures as he speaks during a news conference at the Pentagon on November 10, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. U.S. Rep. Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth on Monday, saying he violated the Constitution by waging war in Iran without congressional authorization and other charges.
Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images
But according to journalists in the room, a Pentagon official working for Hegseth warned reporters that they would be physically evicted if they got out of line.
âA security agent for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth just warned the reporters hereâfor Hegsethâs first press conference in 6 monthsâthat we will be physically removed from the briefing room if we are not professional and maintain decorum,â Washington Post correspondent Tara Copp wrote on X, alongside a photo of the briefing room this morning.
Tara Copp from the Washington Post reported the threat from the Pentagon briefing room.
âWe asked if that meant no shouted questions and got no clarity. Itâs the first time any of us could ever remember being threatened like this. Shouted questions are normal. âThis is crazy town,â one journalist said, noting the White House has never threatened reporters like that.â
The account was backed up by Vanity Fairâs Washington Correspondent Aidan McLaughlin.
By clicking â SUBSCRIBE â you agree to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy .
âAt Pete Hegsethâs briefing this morning, an official came out to tell reporters that if anyone âgets out of lineâ they will be âremoved physically.â Reporters shouted back âwhat does that mean?â Official said it meant to maintain âdecorumâ and added he was just relaying orders,â McLaughlin posted.
âA few minutes later, DOD press aide Joel Valdez walked out and said he would explain the orders off the record. Reporters asked for it to be on background. Valdez looked down at the floor and then walked out of the room without saying anything.â
The Daily Beast has reached out to the Pentagon for comment on the episode, which fits a broader pattern of press crackdowns under Hegsethâand of his reputation for carefully managing his on-camera image.
Last year, for instance, the Pentagon required reporters to sign off on new rules governing access and information-gathering to obtain a media pass.
Many traditional national security reporters refused to sign on, allowing the expansion of MAGA-friendly outlets across outlets such as Lindell TV (run by conspiracy theorist and My Pillow Guy chief Mike Lindell), Breitbart News, and the Gateway Pundit.
After a mass walkout, much of the Pentagon press corps was replaced by right-wing influencers.
Hegseth also came under fire last year after reports that a green room near the Pentagon briefing area had been modified with mirrors and lighting so officials could prepare for television appearances.
Initial renovation ideas were estimated to cost tens of thousands of dollars before being scaled back, though Hegseth publicly dismissed the coverage as a âfake story.â
A security agent for Hegseth warned journalists to maintain decorum.
And in March this year, the Pentagon reportedly banned some photographers from briefings on Trumpâs war in Iran after Hegsethâs staff found certain photos of the defense secretary âunflattering.â
A spokeswoman for Hegseth also rejected this at the time, telling the Daily Beast that space in the briefing room was limited, so they had to limit the number of uncredentialed photographers.
US Representative Thomas Massie (R-KY) holds a press conference about his resolution to impeach Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC on November 9, 2026.
Mondayâs press conference was the first to be held at the Pentagon since May, and comes a day after Republican Rep. Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth.
These include accusing Hegseth of waging war against Iran without congressional approval, authorizing extrajudicial killings in the Caribbean Sea, kidnapping a sovereign foreign leader in Venezuela, and waging an unlawful war in Yemen.
Last year, Donald Trump told reporters at the Oval Office the U.S. had "shot out a drug-carrying boat" coming from Venezuela.
Notably, one article also accuses Hegseth of suppressing free speech by weaponizing the Department of Defense to intimidate and attempt to prosecute U.S. Senator Mark Kelly.
Kelly, a former Navy captain and astronaut, is one of the six Democrats that Hegseth and Trump accused of âseditionâ last year after they appeared in a video reminding service members they could refuse illegal orders.
Kelly said Hegseth needed to be impeached, pointing to the lethal strikes against drug boats and the Iran war as âjust the tip of the iceberg.â
He added that the way the Pentagon chief had also sought to impose his own culture wars on the military, along with his mass firings and his bizarre obsession with testosterone, was like ânothing Iâve ever seen before.
âThe military doesnât need more testosterone. It needs better leadership right now,â Kelly said at the Crooked Con political conference on Saturday.
Senator Mark Kelly speaks at the National Action Network's annual convention on April 11, 2026, in New York City.
David Dee Delgado/David Dee Delgado, Getty Images
But Hegseth strongly defended his record on Monday, telling reporters he was following Trumpâs orders and describing the efforts against him as a political stunt by a disgruntled Republican.
âThis is not oversight, and itâs not accountability. Itâs a political spectacle, a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment,â he said of Massie.
